statement.p: Consider f (x) = a(1 - e^{-bx}) for a>0 and b>0.
Based on your expression for f'(x), is f(x) increasing or decreasing? (Enter increasing or decreasing.)

p.em: (Be sure that you can see why this is true for all values of x.)

statement.p: Based on your expression for f''(x), is f(x) concave up or concave down? (Enter up or down.)

p.em: (Be sure that you can see why this is true for all values of x.)

static.solution:
f(x) = a - a e^{-b x}, we find its derivative using the chain rule: f'(x) = ab e^{-b x}. Exponentials are always positive, so that, given that a > 0 and b > 0, we must have f'(x) > 0 and we know that f(x) must be increasing.
Then f''(x) = -a b^2 e^{-b x} \lt 0, so the function must be concave down.
